title: Agent harness registry row
description: How to recognise one agent harness on macOS and tell whether it is working. Rows are data: adding a harness never needs a code change. Every non-obvious field must be backed by an entry in sources.

surfaces.description: Each way the harness runs: a terminal UI, a desktop app, an IDE extension, a background daemon.

process.description: Matching reads the command line only. names is compared with the base name of argv[0]; path_contains with argv[0] itself; args_contain must each appear in some argument; exclude_args vetoes on an exact argument. The executable path is not used: a harness may run bundled tools from its own binary under another name. names and path_contains are alternatives (either is enough); a longer path match is more specific, and when a process matches two rows it belongs to the more specific one.

session_id_args.description: Flags whose value is the session id, used to map a process to its own transcript.

hosts_agents.description: This surface runs agents of other rows as its children (an orchestrator or host app: Emdash, Conductor, T3 Code). A process of another row that has a matched process of this surface above it is folded into that ancestor: only the ancestor is reported, and it reads working while the hosted agent does. Set it only where the row's evidence says the host launches claude, codex or the like itself. Leave it off for a multiplexer or terminal host where the user starts agents by hand (herdr, agent-deck, claude-squad, superset): those sessions keep their own row. Not to be confused with host, which says one process holds many sessions.

presence.description: Paths, ~ and globs allowed. A surface match that rests on a bare name (the process name matched and no path_contains entry did) counts only when at least one of these exists. Use it where the name is shared with another program (a JSON viewer called fx, AWS Copilot called copilot) and take the path from the row's own session_store or install layout. A match through a path_contains entry is never held back. Absent: no guard.

glob.description: Shell glob for transcript files, ~ allowed.

per_session.description: Path template with {session_id} when a process can be mapped to one file.

documented.description: False when the path is observed but never promised by the vendor.

working_signals.description: Any one of these being true means a turn is in progress. Ordered most precise first. child_process and tool_children look at DIRECT children only; tool_children counts shells; power_assertion may carry name to match the assertion's name; a transcript write can raise working but its absence never proves idle.

args_contain.description: child_process only. Every entry must be an argument of the child (exact match). For -w, the argument after it must be the pid of the matched process, which is how `caffeinate -i -w <pid>` shows that the inhibitor belongs to that process and no other.

waiting_signals.description: How to tell the agent is blocked on the human (permission prompt, question). Often hooks only.

evidence.description: A URL, a file path in the vendor's source, or the exact local command and what it printed.

confidence.description: verified-locally: the probe classified a real running instance correctly. documented: vendor docs or source say so. inferred: third-party reports only.

no_outside_signal.description: True when nothing outside the process can say whether it is working (no per-thread signal, a client of cloud work). With no signal fired the state is unknown, not idle. Unknown is counted on its own, never as working or idle. Absent: idle.
